newsitem.title: USA: IGG Intl compound impact demonstrated.
newsitem.headline: IGG Intl compound impact demonstrated.

text.p: IGG International Inc said Wednesday greenhouse experiments conducted on the company's lead agricultural compound, Elexa, demonstrated that this naturally derived carbohydrate compound defends a wide range of crops from attack from many types of fungi.

"We are very excited about the results from these experiments," stated the researcher, Dr. Noach Ben-Shalom of the Agricultural Research Organization, Volcani Institute in Israel. "Elexa is the first compound we have tested that works on such a broad range of fungi without having toxic effects on the plants."

Results from the greenhouse experiments demonstrate that Elexa is highly effective in controlling fungal diseases on cucumber, potato, and tomato plants, IGG said. Seven days after treatment with a 0.1 percent solution of Elexa, about 80 percent of the crops were free of disease compared to zero percent for non-treated control.

The company said it has initiated multiple field tests on grapes, tomatoes, potatoes, rice and other vegetable crops to confirm Elexa's efficacy under normal growing conditions. The results of these studies are expected in the fourth quarter.
